location: Nauvis - Crash Site - Iron Ore Deposit #2
summary: Today was mostly spent gathering stone and expanding the perimeter. I managed to research enough additional chunk claim points to lay out a 7x9 rectangle for the base perimeter. I still don’t have enough points to claim the interior fully, but it’s a decent starting size.
Turrets and walls are up on all sides, though gaps remain. I’d like to think I’m relatively safe for now. Maybe one day I’ll have enough resources to complete a full defensive perimeter.

Resource-wise, like I mentioned, A lot of stone mining was required — both for the perimeter foundation and to keep science running. I lost count of how many rocks I chipped today, but it was significant. Thankfully, the southern and western sides of the crash site are rich in stone, so luck is on my side there.
Science made substantial progress. Beyond the additional chunk research, I completed Fuel Processing, Electricity, and Basic Water Processing.

Fuel Processing allows me to convert raw coal into processed fuel with a 10% energy boost. Raw coal is weak at 1.5MJ and burns fast, producing a lot of ash. Processed fuel doesn’t produce ash when burned, which helps centralize ash production, but unfortunately, only burner generators can use it, so raw coal still powers most machines.

Electricity was a major milestone. I can now craft small electric poles, eliminating the need to manually relocate the burner generator. I can also produce additional burner generators, so losing the only one won’t strand me.
Basic Water Processing converts raw water into clean water suitable for delicate machines. I don’t have an immediate application yet, but future plans include boilers for steam production.

In addition, I expanded iron production. A second iron furnace stack is now online, supported by new miners dedicated to feeding it. This should help meet growing demand for iron plates in both production and science.
Tomorrow’s goal will likely be designing a new setup for fuel processing and burner generators to improve efficiency and centralize operations.
